clue.text: He spreads the word to the heathen during Torpids with difficulty

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time span of the other, so it goes inside
something done with difficulty is struggled over and muddled, so the letters of Torpids are worked into a new order

parts.note: a heathen is a pagan, a non-believer

explanation.surface: A missionary preaches to unbelievers in the middle of a hard-fought Oxford boat race.
explanation.walkthrough: Torpids are Oxford University's college rowing races, held early in the year. 'with difficulty' turns the race name into PRODIST, and 'during' puts the heathen inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagandist is someone who spreads a message or doctrine, as a preacher spreads the gospel.

clue.text: Like a royal residence, it repels one of taste

indicators.note: to repel is to drive away, so the letter for one is pushed out of the word

parts.note: a royal residence is a palace, and something like one is palatial
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A palace that turns away anyone with refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' is a link referring back to the palatial word, which repels the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatal relates to the palate, the roof of the mouth long regarded as the seat of the sense of flavour.

clue.text: Fail to keep fit?

parts.note: reads like failing to stay in shape, but means getting too big for one's clothes so that they no longer fit

explanation.definitionFit: When a child gets too big for a garment, the garment stops fitting them.

clue.text: Silver company with minor trouble about the best use of land

definitions.text: about the best use of land

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up and disturb, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A silverware firm with a small problem concerning how best to farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition, meaning 'concerning'; 'trouble' shuffles the company and minor into RONOMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production, so agronomic means concerned with getting the most from farmland.

clue.text: Platforms for the great Cham — Boswell'S contribution

indicators.note: the letters are a part given by the words before, a share they contribute

explanation.surface: Boswell supplies a stage for Dr Johnson, nicknamed the great Cham, to hold forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson was called 'the great Cham' (khan) of literature, and James Boswell was his biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early Christian churches, so ambos are raised stands for speakers.

clue.text: Writer's devil

definitions.meaning: used in exclamations like 'what the ...?', where it stands for the devil

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the novelist of Oliver Twist; the other is an old euphemism for Satan in oaths.

clue.text: Little ladybird in sea water pool

parts.note: read as 'little lady' plus 'bird': Sal, a pet form of Sally, is a little lady
the bird hiding at the end of 'ladybird' is a tern, a seabird

explanation.surface: A tiny ladybird has fallen into a rock pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The split runs through the middle of 'ladybird': the insect is a decoy, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltern is a set of pools where seawater evaporates to leave salt.

clue.text: It's used to waterproof what sounds like a top-hole club

indicators.note: the phrase says the first part is a word spoken that matches another in sound

parts.note: top-hole is old British slang for excellent, as is corking
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A gadget for making things watertight seems to be named after a first-rate golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-hole' and 'corking' are both dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A caulking iron is a chisel-like tool for driving oakum into the seams of a wooden ship to seal it.

clue.text: What a heavenly cast!

parts.note: a cast in the sky would be made of stars, and a film whose cast is all famous names is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is one made up entirely of celebrated performers.

clue.text: The dollar was ahead, then collapsed

parts.note: buck is slang for a dollar
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Currency markets: the dollar led and then crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that buckled gave way under pressure and folded.

clue.text: What sort of horsepower does this auxiliary motor have?

definitions.text: What sort of horsepower does this auxiliary motor have?

parts.words: What sort of horsepower does this auxiliary motor have?
parts.note: plays on horsepower as if the engine were powered by an animal, a small beast of burden rather than a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A donkey engine is a small auxiliary steam engine on a ship, used for pumping or hoisting.

clue.text: A comparatively recent article in the Roman church

parts.note: later is the comparative of late, meaning more recent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.definitionFit: St John Lateran is the cathedral of Rome, the Pope's own church as bishop of the city.

clue.text: Governor and bishop seen hanging around liquor shop

indicators.note: the outer word hangs round the others, holding them inside it

parts.note: taken as written
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Officials and clergy are spotted loitering near a drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: HE for His Excellency is the crossword's stock colonial governor; 'hanging around' wraps the word seen round both officials.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking house selling illicit spirits.

clue.text: Relative better at home than out

definitions.text: Relative better at home than out

parts.words: Relative better at home than out
parts.note: a family member by marriage is called 'in' something; swap the in for out and you have a fugitive criminal

explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's parent or sibling is related by marriage, and the 'out' version is a bandit.

clue.text: You have to be reasonable to combine fashion with taste

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
taste is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Sensible advice to blend style with good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: When something adds up logically it is coherent and reasonable.

clue.text: Bird hears the cat's on holiday

indicators.note: what one hears is the spoken sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a cat is a kitty, and a wake is a local holiday in northern England

explanation.surface: A bird learns that the cat is away, so it is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Wakes weeks were annual holidays in northern English mill towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small cliff-nesting gull of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: A surprising cry for the celebrated romancer to utter

indicators.note: uttering is speaking aloud, so the phrase is a sound match

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, the famous author of historical romances, is a great Scott

explanation.surface: An exclamation fitting for a famous novelist to say.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott wrote Ivanhoe and Waverley, romances in the old sense of adventure tales.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dated exclamation of astonishment, like 'good heavens!'.

clue.text: Paper (or paste) maker

indicators.note: a maker builds something new, so these letters are made into another word

explanation.surface: A manufacturer of paper or glue.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the fodder inside what looks like an aside about glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto grass is used to make fine paper, so the word can stand for the material of paper.

clue.text: This member is horizontal by the window

definitions.text: This member is horizontal by the window

parts.words: This member is horizontal by the window
parts.note: member reads as a person but is a structural piece of timber, a crossbar set at a window

explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar in a window frame or above a door.

clue.text: Fool about in the sand

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone messing about on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' signals C going inside DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, a dolt.

clue.text: Conveyance as drawn up in Moscow, perhaps

definitions.text: Conveyance as drawn up in Moscow, perhaps

parts.words: Conveyance as drawn up in Moscow, perhaps
parts.note: a conveyance sounds like a legal deed drawn up, but here it is a vehicle pulled up by horses in Russia

explanation.definitionFit: A droshky is a low four-wheeled open Russian carriage.

clue.text: Venetia represents simplicity

indicators.note: to re-present is to present again in a new form, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Venetia stands for innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent artlessness, a lack of worldly guile.

clue.text: Put back in right plane after changing

indicators.note: the word is altered into a new order of letters

parts.note: the setter meant 'planet', which supplies the T the printed word lacks

explanation.surface: Restore something to the correct surface once it has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder is one letter short; 'planet' gives EPLANT after 'after changing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To replant is to set a plant in the soil again after lifting it.

clue.text: Arms may be held in this position for the track

definitions.text: Arms may be held in this position
definitions.meaning: the drill command '... arms' has a rifle held at the side parallel to the ground
a path or trace left behind

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a military rifle carry; the other is a beaten path through country.

clue.text: What my darling was for ever dashing away at tunefully

definitions.text: What my darling was for ever dashing away at tunefully

parts.words: What my darling was for ever dashing away at tunefully
parts.note: recalls the English folk song 'Dashing Away with the Smoothing Iron', in which the singer's darling presses clothes every day

explanation.definitionFit: The song's sweetheart is pressing laundry with a hot iron each day of the week.

clue.text: Shakespearian maid who returns in the guise of Circe

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: as means in the role or guise of
Circe, the enchantress of the Odyssey, is a temptress, a siren

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare servant comes back on stage dressed as Circe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's waiting-woman in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Old Greek poet in current Dynasty

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: in places the poet within the other letters

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled China
AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George Russell

explanation.surface: A poet appears in a modern television soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynasty was a 1980s American TV soap, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achaeans were Greeks of Homer's epics, and the word is used for the ancient Greek people generally.

clue.text: The ceremonial keys to the park are kept in this

parts.note: something ceremonial is formal
D and E are musical keys
Hyde Park is the great royal park in central London

explanation.surface: A ceremonial set of keys to the park is stored here.
explanation.walkthrough: Specimens are preserved in a solution of this chemical, which is why things 'are kept in this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Formaldehyde in solution is the classic preservative for biological specimens.
